sections.html:
Winchester is Virginia's northernmost independent city, in the Shenandoah Valley between the Blue Ridge and the Allegheny mountains. The 2020 census counted 28,120 people, with an estimate of 28,272 for 2025. Housing units numbered 12,372, and 7.8 percent of them were vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 2.0 percent.

The city is the county seat of Frederick County but is its own jurisdiction, with separate offices and separate tax bills. A house with a Winchester mailing address can sit inside the city or out in the county. Before you chase any tax question, find out which government assesses and bills your parcel.

Interstate 81 runs through town, which matters to commuters. Washington, D.C. is roughly 75 miles east, and Martinsburg, West Virginia is 24 miles north. Buyers who work out of town will ask about drive times.

Winchester dates to 1744 and calls itself the oldest Virginia city west of the Blue Ridge. The Winchester Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places, covers buildings from 1750 to 1930. City law penalizes work on historic properties done without approval.

If your house is old and you plan exterior repairs before selling, ask the Planning and Zoning office at Rouss City Hall, 15 N. Cameron Street, whether your address is in the district. Get approval first. Tell any buyer about the exterior approval rules early so the rules do not come as a surprise at inspection.

sections.h2: Real estate tax rate and due dates
sections.html:
The Commissioner of the Revenue sets the assessment as of January 1 each year. The Treasurer collects the money in two payments.

ChargeAmount or dateNotes
Tax rate$0.795 per $100 of assessed valueCan change when the city adopts its budget
Due datesJune 5 and December 5Next business day if either falls on a weekend
Late penalty10 percentAdded the day after the due date
Interest10 percent a yearCharged daily after the penalty is assessed

The Treasurer's office is in the Creamery Building, 21 S. Kent St., Suite 101, open 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. Monday to Friday. If a bill is behind, call the Treasurer before collection action begins and ask about a payment plan. Check the rate again before closing.

Unpaid real estate tax comes out of the sale proceeds. Virginia gives the locality a lien that ranks ahead of other liens, and it stays attached until the money reaches the right tax officer and the Treasurer releases it.

Whoever handles the closing, whether the buyer or a foreclosure trustee, has to apply the proceeds to the tax, penalties and interest first. Your share of the current year is divided by the purchase contract, so read that section of your agreement.

Virginia also allows a court sale of land with delinquent tax after a set period. The Treasurer has to send notice at least 30 days before suing, and property with condemned structures can be reached sooner. If you are behind, a call to the Treasurer is the best first move.

The seller owes the state grantor tax by default, at 50 cents for each $500 of value, though a buyer may agree to pay it. The circuit court clerk will not record a deed unless the price is on its first page. Your closing agent will show the figure on the settlement statement.

Winchester has hot, humid summers and cool winters, with a mean January low of 21.2 degrees Fahrenheit. Inspectors for buyers tend to look hard at gutters, grading, basements and the heating system.

Before you sell, service the furnace or heat pump and keep the paperwork. Clear gutters and downspouts so the inspection report shows fewer water complaints. Fix visible roof damage, since a repair estimate can turn into a price cut.

sections.h2: How a cash sale works here
sections.html:
With no lender involved, the timeline depends on the title search, any open liens and the date you choose. The steps match the rest of Virginia: a signed contract, a title review, payoff of taxes and mortgages from proceeds, and a deed recorded with the circuit court.

Plan around the calendar. The Shenandoah Apple Blossom Festival takes place the first weekend of May, and local schools and many businesses close that Friday, so inspectors and notaries are easier to book in other weeks.

Gather your last tax bill and any mortgage statement. List known repairs, since a cash buyer prices the house as it stands. On the days before closing, ask the Treasurer for the tax balance as of your closing date, and confirm the payoff with your lender in writing.

A cash sale also skips buyer financing, so you avoid waiting on a bank appraisal or loan approval. If the buyer is paying all cash, the main steps left are title work, signing and recording.

faqs.q: What is the Winchester real estate tax rate?
faqs.a: The rate is $0.795 per $100 of assessed value, with taxes due June 5 and December 5. The Treasurer's Office collects them, and the rate can change with the city budget.

faqs.q: Is Winchester part of Frederick County for tax purposes?
faqs.a: No. Winchester is an independent city and the county seat, but it is a separate jurisdiction. The city assesses and bills property inside its limits, and Frederick County handles property outside them.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Winchester property tax late?
faqs.a: The city adds a 10 percent penalty the day after the due date, then charges 10 percent interest a year, daily, once the penalty is added. The Treasurer can set up a payment plan before collection action starts.

faqs.q: Do I need approval to repair an older house in Winchester?
faqs.a: It depends on whether the property is in the Historic Winchester District. Work on historic properties without approval is penalized, so ask Planning and Zoning before changing the outside of an older house.

faqs.q: Who pays the Virginia deed tax when a house is sold?
faqs.a: By default the seller, as the grantor, pays the state grantor tax of 50 cents for each $500 of value. The buyer and seller can agree that the buyer pays some or all of it.
